skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: Cleared reusable generic skin atlas; not a likeness, attested complexion, or source identifying any named/reconstructed resident.
skin_texture.uv_status: Source atlas and UV registration viewed in source diagnostics; final Blender export/LOD render validation remains outstanding.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Shared cleared CC0 short04 source fitted to existing Otis/Joseph/Martin bodies; hair/part/color are reconstructed choices, no period hairstyle attestation or individual likeness.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed unbreeched child of the 1812 town, boy or girl of about two and a half to four and a half, in a white high-waisted short-sleeved cotton frock to the ankle, red shoes, bare head, on a 3-year child body of the shared portable rig
basis: Original garments on a cleared MakeHuman hm08 child body (T-3465): shells offset from the body's own surface, a skirt lofted round its own sections, pieces cut from a garment's own surface, after the period pictures named in the sources and the children's research (docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3465/day.json "dress"; docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json "Children 2-12 and infants"). Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing.
source_scope: Eastern portraits and objects of about 1805-1815 (the Met): Joshua Johnson's Rutter children and Emma Van Name (Baltimore, about 1805), the Beecher child's frock (about 1813), the Pixler family (about 1815). None shows a child at Chicago; Wau-Bun and Quaife place the children in the town and record nothing of their dress. No pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

reference_summary.name: an unbreeched child of the 1812 town, boy or girl, about two and a half to four and a half

body_parameters.height_basis: CDC 2000 stature-for-age, boys, 10th centile at 36.5 months (90.5 cm; statage.csv; the girls' 89.2 cm is drawn by the kit's scale, and the preparation tool's floor is 0.90 m), the centile the children's research (T-3465) takes for every child of 1812. The kit draws each child at their own height (0.88-1.12 of this: about 0.80-1.01 m). Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at 3 of either sex (MakeHuman baby 7/9, child 2/9 between its 1- and 10-year anchors, male and female targets equally); no child of the town is named by the asset and no age is read. Stands for children about 2 to 4.7 at the 10th centile; see the notes file.
body_parameters.shape_basis: CC0 male and female child and baby macro targets in equal share; equal software-category blend is engineering only, not inferred ancestry or a portrait.

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 child graphical body and a cleared generic young skin atlas are reconstructed authoring choices. The child is anonymous: a child of the town whose presence Quaife (1913, App. IX) and Wau-Bun record, not any one of them; no complexion, height, face or outfit of anyone is asserted.

child_components.evidence_choice: The research puts unbreeched children of either sex, about 1 to 4, in white high-waisted frocks to the ankle (the Beecher frock was a boy's); infants in arms are not drawn (no carry pose), so this is the youngest asset, worn by the children who walk.

provenance.source_scope: A white cotton frock, high waist and short puffed sleeves: the Beecher frock (about 1813), worn by an infant boy, and the Rutter girl's, so boys and girls alike. Neck and sleeve cut reconstructed.
To the ankle (the Rutter girl). Fullness reconstructed; the Beecher frock's embroidered hem is not made.
Red shoes on both of Joshua Johnson's small children (about 1805); the shared closed shoe stands for a soft leather shoe. A frontier toddler barefoot in August is as likely and not made.
